expect.note: `POST /tasks` takes a per-task mode flag (ADR-027 Decision 1). Absent means the env default, which is mode B; `loop` reaches `live_driver` and not `live_planner`; anything else is refused before a run exists. The factories are recorded from the eval side — a flag that is accepted and silently ignored looks identical over HTTP to one that works, which is exactly how the M9 ablation nearly measured one model four times (PR #15).

provenance: M42/ADR-028. The `factory` column is the half nothing else can see: without it this case would pass with the mode field parsed, validated and dropped.
provenance_drift_2026_08_26: Spec-drift audit finding 3, watched red: `_execute` passed `t.model or DEFAULT_MODEL` whatever the mode, so a loop-mode request with no explicit model drove the loop with `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` — the model ADR-010's COST ablation picked under a ceiling ADR-027 deliberately lifted for this mode. `DEFAULT_LOOP_MODEL` existed, was documented as 'the loop driver's default', and was dead in production: every call site overrode it. The consequence is not cosmetic — ADR-028 §6 justifies the USD ceiling by 'loop mode calls a frontier model once per step', and §8 records `input_modalities: image` and `supported_parameters: tools` for `claude-opus-5` and for nothing else, so the model that would actually have run was never verified to support the tool-calling the driver requires. The last row is the other direction: an EXPLICIT model still wins over the mode default, because the ablation and any future A/B need to pin the model themselves.
